findings.why: Returning an empty default from a catch block can hide a real failure behind a plausible value.
findings.suggestedAction: Use an explicit error path or document and justify the fallback at the boundary.

findings.message: Found PHP catch block that flattens the caught exception into generic string data
findings.why: Flattening caught exception text into ordinary return or payload data blurs success and failure paths and loses typed failure context.
findings.suggestedAction: Preserve the exception path or map it to a deliberate typed/domain error result instead of generic string data.

findings.message: Found near-duplicate PHP function bodies
findings.why: Near-identical bodies across multiple functions often come from copy-paste evolution.
findings.suggestedAction: Review whether the shared logic should move into one helper or a clearer abstraction.

findings.message: Found PHP catch block that logs or prints and continues
findings.why: Logging or printing an error and then continuing can turn a broken path into a silent failure.
findings.suggestedAction: Stop execution, return an explicit fallback, or rethrow after logging.
evidence: catch body logs/prints without throw or return
